title: Strings Toolkit: Windows, Palindromes, KMP, Rabin-Karp and Tries
summary: Quick revision notes on the string algorithms interviews lean on: sliding windows with frequency counts, palindrome expansion, KMP, Rabin-Karp rolling hash and tries. Each chapter gives the model, the pattern, the complexity and the usual bugs.

chapters.title: Sliding Window and Frequency Counts
points: Sliding window keeps a range [l, r] over the string and updates state incrementally as r grows and l shrinks, giving O(n) instead of O(n^2) re-scanning
Fixed-size window: add s[r], drop s[r-k] once the window is longer than k; variable window: expand r, then shrink l while the window is invalid
Longest substring without repeats: store the last index of each char in a map and jump l to max(l, last[c]+1), O(n) time, O(alphabet) space
Anagram check or find all anagrams: compare a 26-slot count array (or a map) of window vs pattern; track a matched counter so each slide is O(1) instead of re-comparing arrays
Mistakes: moving l backwards when jumping to a last-seen index (use max), not removing a count of zero from a map before comparing, and updating the answer before the window is valid

chapters.title: Palindromes and Expand Around Centre
points: A palindrome reads the same both ways; a string of length n has 2n-1 centres (n single chars for odd length, n-1 gaps between chars for even length)
Expand around centre: for each centre set l and r, then while l>=0, r<n and s[l]==s[r] move l-- and r++; O(n^2) time, O(1) space
Longest palindromic substring: run expand(i,i) and expand(i,i+1), keep the best (start, length); length = r-l-1 after the loop ends
Count palindromic substrings: add 1 for every successful expansion step from each of the 2n-1 centres, so the total is O(n^2) worst case

Compare with alternatives: DP table is O(n^2) space, Manacher is O(n) time but harder to code; two-pointer check from both ends tests one whole string in O(n). Common bug: forgetting the even-length centre

chapters.title: KMP and the Prefix Function
points: KMP finds pattern P in text T in O(n+m) by never moving the text pointer backwards; naive matching is O(n*m) in the worst case
Prefix function (LPS) array: lps[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of P[0..i] that is also a suffix of it; for P="ababaca" lps=[0,0,1,2,3,0,1]
Build LPS in O(m): keep length k of the current match; on mismatch set k=lps[k-1] while k>0, on match k++, then store lps[i]=k
Search: on mismatch at pattern index j, set j=lps[j-1] and keep the text index i; when j==m a match ends at i, record i-m+1 and set j=lps[j-1] to find overlapping matches

Mistakes: resetting j to 0 on mismatch, treating the whole pattern as its own prefix (the prefix must be proper), and skipping the j=lps[j-1] step after a full match. Trick: lps also gives the shortest repeating period m-lps[m-1]

chapters.title: Rabin-Karp Rolling Hash
points: Rabin-Karp hashes each length-m window of the text and compares it to the pattern hash, then verifies on a hash match; expected O(n+m), worst case O(n*m)
Polynomial hash: h = s[0]*B^(m-1) + ... + s[m-1], taken mod a large prime M; precompute B^(m-1) mod M for the roll
Rolling update in O(1): h = ((h - s[i]*B^(m-1)) * B + s[i+m]) mod M; add M before the final mod so the value never goes negative
Always compare the actual substrings after a hash hit, because collisions cause false positives; use a large prime modulus or a double hash to make them rare
Best fit: searching many patterns of equal length, or duplicate-substring detection with a hash set. Compared with KMP, it is simpler to extend but has no worst-case guarantee

chapters.title: Tries for Prefix Search
points: A trie is a tree where each edge is a character and each node marks whether a word ends there; the shared prefixes are stored only once
Insert and search cost O(L) for a word of length L, independent of how many words are stored; children are stored as a 26-slot array or a hash map
startsWith(prefix) walks the prefix path and returns true if every node exists; search(word) also needs the end-of-word flag to be true
Autocomplete: walk to the prefix node, then DFS its subtree to collect every word, optionally capped at top-k
Mistakes: returning true from search for a prefix that is not a full word, array children wasting memory on sparse alphabets (use a map), and forgetting the end-of-word flag when deleting a word

chapters.title: String Algorithms Cheat Sheet
points: Sliding window: O(n) time; fixed size is add right and drop left, variable is expand then shrink while invalid; count array of 26 for lowercase letters
Palindrome: 2n-1 centres, expand while s[l]==s[r], O(n^2) time and O(1) space, length = r-l-1
KMP: lps[i] = longest proper prefix that is also a suffix; on mismatch j=lps[j-1]; O(n+m); period = m-lps[m-1]
Rabin-Karp: roll h=((h-s[i]*B^(m-1))*B+s[i+m]) mod M; verify on a hash match; expected O(n+m), worst case O(n*m)

Trie: insert, search and startsWith are O(L); search needs the end flag; pick by need: window for substrings with a constraint, KMP for single exact pattern, Rabin-Karp for multi-pattern or duplicates, trie for prefix queries
